page: Microsoft Azure D32lds_v7 is a compute-optimized virtual machine running on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor. It features 32 dedicated vCPUs mapped to 16 physical cores of an Intel Xeon 6973P-C processor operating at 4.2 GHz. The architecture is x86_64, supported by a large 480 MB L3 cache. This instance is configured with 64.0 GB of system memory, yielding a low memory-to-vCPU ratio of 2.0 GB per vCPU. It includes a bundled local storage disk of 1890 GB and is Premium Storage capable.

Benchmark data highlights strong performance in specific vector and compression tasks. The single-threaded gzip compression reaches 35.44 GB/sec, and multi-threaded bzip3 decompression achieves 202.24 GB/sec, both placing in the top 25% tier. Static web serving throughput is also strong at 54.89 GB/sec. For machine learning workloads, the CPU's Advanced Matrix Extensions (AMX) support top-tier text generation speeds of 346.08 tokens/sec for small 135M models, though performance drops to an average 24.76 tokens/sec for medium 7B models. General compute and memory bandwidth benchmarks, such as stress-ng and Passmark CPU scores, consistently register in the average range.

The primary tradeoff of the D32lds_v7 is its low memory density relative to its high compute capacity. With only 2 GB of RAM per vCPU, it is less suitable for memory-intensive databases or massive in-memory data processing. However, the combination of a high-frequency 4.2 GHz CPU, dedicated cores, and a substantial 1890 GB local storage allocation makes it highly cost-efficient for compute-heavy workloads that do not require large memory footprints. Suitable workloads include web serving, batch processing, software compilation, and lightweight machine learning inference.
